speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your knee pain and swelling, could you tell me your age and sex? I also need to know if you have experienced any fever, chills, or recent urinary symptoms like burning or frequency.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the combination of your recent urinary symptoms, the migratory pattern of your joint swelling, and your sexual history, I suspect an infection-related arthritis. REQUEST TEST: Urine NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal urine test results make a typical sexually transmitted infection less likely, but they do not rule out reactive arthritis, which can occur even without detectable bacteria in the urine at the time of testing. To further evaluate this possibility, do you have any history of recent eye redness or pain (conjunctivitis/uveitis) or skin changes like psoriasis?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of recent eye redness or pain, or any skin changes like psoriasis? I also need to know if you have had any recent gastrointestinal infections, such as diarrhea or abdominal pain.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported. Social history: Sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your social history, but I still need to rule out other causes for your joint and urinary symptoms. Have you experienced any recent gastrointestinal issues like diarrhea, or do you have any current eye redness or skin rashes?

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see. Given your history of inconsistent condom use and urinary symptoms, I need to confirm if there is an ongoing urethritis. REQUEST TEST: Urine Gram Stain and Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein Negative, Blood Negative, WBC 12–16/hpf, RBC 1–2/hpf

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis showing white blood cells confirms urethritis, which, combined with your migratory arthritis and sexual history, strongly suggests reactive arthritis. I will now request imaging to assess the joint inflammation. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a young male with urethritis (pyuria), migratory oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), and a history of inconsistent condom use is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis, even with a negative initial NAAT which can occur due to timing or prior antibiotic use. The absence of eye symptoms or skin changes does not rule it out, as the classic triad is present in only a minority of cases. DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis
